b2-23-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Sudden Reaction
b2-23-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how you reacted when you heard some very good news. You were so happy that you started to laugh at once.
b2-23-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how you reacted to the good news.
cues: Say that you suddenly started to laugh
b2-23-01.target: Cuando oí la buena noticia, me eché a reír.
b2-23-01.english: When I heard the good news, I burst out laughing.
b2-23-01.canDo: I can use *echarse a* + infinitive for a sudden reaction such as crying, laughing or running.

b2-23-02.title: Communicative Challenge: After Dinner
b2-23-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you did after dinner yesterday. You sat down and started to read a book.
b2-23-02.prompt: Tell Meg what you did after dinner.
cues: Say that you set about reading
b2-23-02.target: Después de cenar, me puse a leer un libro.
b2-23-02.english: After dinner, I started reading a book.
b2-23-02.canDo: I can use *ponerse a* + infinitive to say that someone sets about a task, a reaction or a change in the weather.

b2-23-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The End of the Concert
b2-23-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what happened at the end of a concert. After a moment of silence, everyone started to applaud.
b2-23-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened at the end of the concert.
cues: Say that there was a silence first
b2-23-03.target: Después de un momento de silencio, todos rompieron a aplaudir.
b2-23-03.english: After a moment of silence, everyone burst into applause.
b2-23-03.canDo: I can use *romper a* + infinitive for sounds, tears and rain that burst out.

b2-23-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Promise
b2-23-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg says you were late for the last meeting and asks if it will happen again. You promise it will not.
b2-23-04.prompt: Promise Meg that you will not be late again.
cues: Say that you will not be late again
b2-23-04.target: Te prometo que no volveré a llegar tarde.
b2-23-04.english: I promise you I will not be late again.
b2-23-04.canDo: I can use *volver a* + infinitive to say that something happens again.

b2-23-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Next Part
b2-23-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what comes next in your talk. You have finished the first part and now you move on to the second part.
b2-23-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what you will do next in your talk.
cues: Say that the first part is finished
Say that you move on to explain the second part
b2-23-05.target: Ya terminé la primera parte; ahora paso a explicar la segunda.
b2-23-05.english: I have finished the first part; now I move on to explain the second.
b2-23-05.canDo: I can use *pasar a* + infinitive to move on to the next step of a talk, a task or a career.

b2-23-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Busy Morning
b2-23-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how your morning went. You started working early, then moved on to your messages, and you did not look at your phone again until noon.
b2-23-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg how your morning went.
cues: Say that you set about working early
Say what you moved on to afterwards
Say that you did not look at your phone again
b2-23-consolidation.target: Me puse a trabajar temprano y después pasé a leer mis mensajes. No volví a mirar el teléfono hasta el mediodía.
b2-23-consolidation.english: I set about working early and then moved on to reading my messages. I did not look at my phone again until noon.
b2-23-consolidation.canDo: I can tell the sudden starts (*echarse a*, *ponerse a*, *romper a*) apart and choose the right one.
